**A tensor-only format avoids the arbitrary object deserialization used by general pickle files.** Safetensors describes tensor metadata and byte ranges, allowing a loader to access weights without reconstructing arbitrary Python objects. That removes pickle's arbitrary-code mechanism from this format. [1](https://huggingface.co/docs/safetensors/index)

Memory mapping can expose file-backed regions and avoid eagerly copying every tensor. It does not eliminate reading bytes from storage when needed or transferring them into GPU memory.

**Benchmark explicit loading paths.** Cold disk access, warm page cache, sharded files, and selected-tensor access can produce very different timings. Modern PyTorch loading options also include restricted weight loading and memory mapping, so “ten times faster” needs a defined comparison rather than a universal claim.

Verify artifact provenance, integrity, shapes, and resource requirements. A safer tensor format does not establish that model behavior is trustworthy or that unrelated repository code is safe. Report cold and warm load time separately and include device transfer if the operational question is time until a model can serve requests.

**Technical details and references.**

Safetensors stores tensor metadata and contiguous byte ranges without arbitrary Python object deserialization. Memory mapping allows access to file-backed regions and can avoid eager copies or loading unused tensors; actual device transfer still must move bytes into GPU memory. This removes pickle's arbitrary-code execution mechanism from the tensor format. [1](https://huggingface.co/docs/safetensors/index)

A tenfold speedup is workload-specific, depending on storage, page cache, sharding, access patterns, and the loading path. Modern `torch.load` also offers options such as restricted weight loading and memory mapping, so compare explicit configurations. A safe tensor format does not make model outputs trustworthy or eliminate all parser, resource-exhaustion, or repository-code risks. Verify artifact integrity, shapes, and provenance and benchmark cold and warm loads separately rather than reporting cached-file timing as disk throughput.
